metric.diagnostics.method: Compiled a representative program derived from ADV-01_C.zig with zig 0.16.0 build/run and captured raw compiler diagnostics.
observations: Compile-time diagnostics for @intCast catch narrowing/overflow at compile time for comptime-known values, with precise file:line:column, a caret-annotated excerpt, and message naming both the offending value and target type.
Error output includes a 'referenced by' inlining/call trace aiding localization through generic/inlined call chains.

Runtime safety builds (Debug/ReleaseSafe) produce panics with backtrace and source location for detectable UB (integer overflow, bounds, null unwrap), relevant to the ADV-01..ADV-26 adversarial UB corpus.

Weaknesses: comptime error chains can cascade/verbose for generic instantiation failures; evolving stdlib API surface (e.g. std.Io.Threaded, std.process.Init.Minimal) across compiler versions produces version-specific diagnostic noise.
metric.diagnostics.raw_output: test1.zig:10:29: error: type 'i32' cannot represent integer value '9223372036854775807' const b: i32 = @intCast(a); referenced-by trace through std.start callMain/callMainWithArgs/posixCallMainAndExit
metric.diagnostics.score_rationale: 78/100: precise source-located compile-time diagnostics catching semantic errors, plus strong runtime safety-check panics with backtraces, offset by verbosity in generic/comptime error chains and version-to-version API churn.

metric.functionality_expressiveness.method: Inspection of assigned Zig adversarial (ADV-01..26) and micro (mb00..mb11) programs under /quidra-benchmark/template/programs/zig, plus compiler probes with zig 0.16.0.
observations: Zig uses comptime generics (comptime parameters, anytype) instead of traits/interfaces; no operator overloading; no exceptions -- error unions with try/catch give explicit but verbose control flow for generic abstraction relative to Rust traits or Kotlin/Swift protocols.
No stable first-class async/await in this build; micro workloads use std.Io.Threaded abstraction instead, reducing concurrency expressiveness relative to Go goroutines or async/await languages.
Comptime metaprogramming allows generic containers/algorithms without runtime cost, a distinctive expressiveness strength observed across micro workloads.
Manual allocator-passing memory management gives fine control but is more verbose than GC languages for common data structure workloads.
Switch expressions and error unions provide reasonable but not maximal expressiveness compared to pattern matching in Rust/Kotlin.
metric.functionality_expressiveness.score_rationale: 58/100: strong comptime/generic metaprogramming and explicit systems control balanced against absence of traits/interfaces, operator overloading, exceptions, and mature async relative to comparison languages.
